This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Vice President Vance campaigned yesterday in Michigan
for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers.
That Senate race is close.
Vance did not talk about the war in Iran or affordability issues.
Vance instead described Rogers' Democratic opponent
as a, quote, "weasel."
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
is an American of Arab descent.
Vice President Vance claimed El-Sayed has an issue with race.
I don't know why he resents the things that he does.
Perhaps it's because he sees them as too white or too proud
or too American.
But what I do know is this, that Michigan deserves better.
Abdul El-Sayed responded by saying that in the US,
Americans don't discriminate against people
for the color of their skin.
He retorted that Vance should not
come to Michigan to lecture him.
The Democratic Senate candidate was campaigning himself
in Michigan yesterday.
El-Sayed was joined by New York Democratic Congresswoman
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
Michigan Public Radio's Russ McNamara has more.
Republican candidate Mike Rogers
has spent much of this campaign attempting to tie El-Sayed
to terrorist groups.
There's been no evidence linking the Democrat to those claims.
Speaking to a crowd of 1,200 people in Marquette,
Congressman Ocasio-Cortez says those attacks
are a distraction.
They want to make this man look very big and scary
on television, because what they think
is that if they can make you scared of him,
then that means you won't listen to him.
The trip to deep red parts of Michigan
is also a showcase for Ocasio-Cortez,
who is a potential 2028 presidential candidate.
For NPR News, I'm Russ McNamara in Marquette.
Officials in Saudi Arabia are postponing or canceling
a slew of high-profile events.
The move comes after Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen
attacked Saudi Arabia's main airport in the capital, Riyadh.
NPR's Aya Batrawi reports they killed and injured
scores of people over the past week.
A summit next week in the Saudi capital, Riyadh,
between the European Union and leaders from six Gulf Arab
states has been canceled.
The European Council did not give a reason why,
but it comes after the suspension of flights
at Riyadh Airport following days of deadly Houthi attacks
on passenger terminals.
Saudi Arabia has also canceled an international golf
tournament slated for November, an electronic music festival,
and pushed back a major tennis slam in Riyadh
to the end of December.
And in its city of Jeddah, the Red Sea Film Festival,
and a star-studded Arab media awards show
have also been postponed or canceled.
These events are important in Saudi Arabia's efforts
to draw on tourists and investments.
Its war against the Houthis in Yemen, however,
is threatening to derail those economic efforts.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
You're listening to NPR News in Washington.
Authorities in Bend, Oregon say three children and a teacher
were killed yesterday in a shooting
at an elementary school.
Another child and another teacher were wounded.
Police in Bend say the shooter was a 16-year-old male.
He was shot and killed by a bystander who had pursued him
into the school.
Patients may soon no longer have the option
of buying their prescription drugs from Canadian pharmacies
to save money.
NPR Sydney Luckin reports on coming changes to import rules.
The US allows people to import a 90-day supply
of pharmaceuticals with a prescription from a doctor
under certain conditions.
And the medicines pass through customs fairly easily,
as long as they are valued below $800.
But a rule change at US Customs and Border Protection
would require more paperwork, a broker, and something
called an entry bond.
That would make the practice more expensive or even
impossible for the estimated 2 million patients who import
medicines for personal use.
The change was originally set to take effect next week,
but has been pushed back to January of next year.
Sydney Luckin, NPR News.
A big storm is sweeping from the Mid-Atlantic up
into New England today.
The National Weather Service cautions
it could bring damaging wind gusts and possibly
a few tornadoes to the region.
California Fire Authorities say the Bryson Fire north of Los
Angeles is growing rapidly.
It's only about 200 acres in size,
but several evacuations have been ordered.
The fire is not contained.
It could grow more.
Forecasters have issued high wind warnings for the area today.
